description:
Curated worked-example repositories. This file is the trust root, on the same terms as widgets/packs.json: an example is admitted only at a full commit SHA, only from a curated owner, and every file it may fetch is pinned by digest here. A branch is never fetched, because a digest pinned against a moving ref verifies nothing.

An example is a RESOURCE -- a workflow document, data and a provenance record -- and declares no node type, so runtimeFetching: "none" in widgets/packs.json does not reach it. That rule governs widget definitions. See docs/experiments/127-examples-as-repositories.md.

governance.fetchPolicy: Only on an explicit practitioner action, never on load. Opening an example tells a server it was opened, which is the same disclosure the basemaps and Overpass make, and it is named in the interface and recorded in the receipt.
governance.verification: Every fetched file is digested with SubtleCrypto and compared to this catalog. A mismatch is a refusal, not a warning.
governance.offline: An example opened once is cached and stays available. Until it is opened it is FETCHABLE rather than AVAILABLE, and the interface must say which.

examples.title: Snow's South London water supply study, 1854

licence.data: CC0-1.0, except geo/sub-districts-csds.geojson which is BSD-2-Clause
licence.source: Public domain. John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 1855.
licence.note: Why this is recorded per example rather than assumed: the mechanism exists so an example may carry terms this project could not adopt. Here the terms are none, because the figures were transcribed from an 1855 publication rather than from HistData (GPL) or causaldata (MIT). One file is an exception and is named in the licence field: the sub-district polygons are redistributed under BSD-2-Clause, which asks for attribution and does not restrict who may receive a map derived from them. That is why this example can carry them where the UK Data Service's sub-district shapefile, whose licence reaches derived datasets, could not be carried by anyone.

examples.description: An investigation and its questions. Deaths per 1,000 people across the 32 sub-districts behind Snow's Table IX, the boundaries themselves as a 33-part study area with every part named, and 1849 against 1854 across Lambeth moving its intake upstream. Four transcribed tables, a georeferenced plate and three traced supply zones, with the terms of each.
examples.notYet: Nothing joins a table to the parts of a study area, so the 32 mortality rates and the 32 named boundaries cannot colour one another. That join is the choropleth this example argues for in prose.
